evidence.quote: Guinea pigs in the wild do not burrow or build nests. Instead, they seek shelter in the burrows of other animals, as well as in crevices and tunnels formed by vegetation. They are social animals and live in small groups, moving together in herds while foraging for grass or other vegetation. They are most active during dawn and dusk, making them crepuscular.
